post.description: Look up the description, units and duty rates of one HTS number.

htsno.description: HTS number, dotted or bare digits (4, 6, 8 or 10 digits), or a `<chapter>:<ordinal>` heading id from `records_list`.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
One HTS line by its number: exports the 4-digit heading's range (`exportList?from=HHHH&to=HHHH.99.99.99`) and returns the matching row in the same shape as `records_list`, with `parent_htsno` computed within the heading. Accepts the dotted form (`8541.43.00.10`) or bare digits (`8541430010`) with 4, 6, 8 or 10 digits, and the `<chapter>:<ordinal>` id that `records_list` gives unnumbered headings (one chapter export). A number the current revision does not carry is `not_found`. Collection contract name: `records/get`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| `indent` | number | Indentation level as the schedule prints it (0 = heading). |
| `other` | string | Column 2 rate of duty, verbatim; empty string where none. |
| `parent_htsno` | string | The nearest preceding numbered row with a smaller `indent` in the same chapter export; null for 4-digit headings and when no such ancestor is in the fetched range. |
| `publication_id` | string | HTS revision name the row was read from (`2026HTSRev21`). |
| `quota_quantity` | string | Quota quantity text when the row carries one; null otherwise (the export sends null or an empty string, both map to null). |

continuation.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page; pins the revision, chapter and row offset.

limit.description:
Rows per page. Default 500; 5000 returns any chapter in one page (chapter 99, the largest, has about 3,350 rows).

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Every HTS line of the current revision, segmented by chapter: `exportList?from=CC00&to=CC99&format=JSON&styles=false` for one two-digit chapter per segment, paged by `limit` rows. Before each page the current revision name is re-read (`reststop/currentRelease`) and compared with the one pinned in the cursor; if it moved the call fails with `invalid_input` and issue code `publication_changed` on `/continuation` instead of mixing revisions (the server always serves the current revision; it ignores `release=`). Chapter 77 is reserved and empty; empty chapters are skipped. Rows are mapped per the collection contract: `htsno` as `source_record_id` (unnumbered headings get `<chapter>:<ordinal>` and a `parent_htsno`), derived `hts_level`, `hs6`, `statistical_suffix`, `chapter`. Collection contract name: `records/list`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `records` as the primary payload key.

post.description: Before or between `records_list` pages to learn the current revision, or to detect that the schedule moved to a new revision.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Cheap version check of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule: the current revision from `reststop/releaseList` (exactly one entry has `status: current`) with its name as `publication_id`, title, publication and effective dates, the previous revision and the publisher's PDF/JSON file URLs. The publisher posts no hash and the API sends no ETag, so `content_hash` and `record_count` are null: `publication_id` is the change key (a new revision every ~2 weeks). Collection contract name: `source/status`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content_hash` | object | Always null: the publisher posts no hash and the API sends no ETag/Last-Modified. Use `publication_id`. |
| `description` | string | `description` as published, e.g. `2026 HTS Revision 21`. |
| `effective_from` | string | `releaseStartDate` normalized to YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `files` | object[] | Publisher file URLs for this revision: the complete HTS PDF (`finalCopy`) and the full-schedule JSON/CSV exports (12.6 MB JSON, 2 to 34 s; `records_list` reads it one chapter at a time instead). |
| `previous_effective_to` | string | `releaseEndDate` of the previous revision, normalized; null when absent. |
| `previous_publication_id` | string | Name of the most recently superseded revision (the archive entry with the latest `releaseEndDate`), null if none. |
| `publication_id` | string | Revision name, e.g. `2026HTSRev21`; the value `records_list` cursors pin. |
| `published_date` | string | Date the revision was published (source `date`, MM/DD/YYYY, normalized to YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `record_count` | object | Always null: counting rows needs the 98 chapter exports; `records_list` reports each segment's `segment_record_count` instead. |
| `retrieved_at` | string |  |
| `revision_count` | number | Number of revisions releaseList enumerates (current plus archive, back to 2015). |
| `segment_key` | string | How `records_list` segments the schedule: one two-digit chapter (`01`..`99`) per segment, `exportList?from=CC00&to=CC99`. |
| `source_url` | string |  |
| `status` | string |  |
| `target_date` | string | `target` (planned effective date) normalized; null when the source leaves it empty. |
| `title` | string | `title` as published, e.g. `Revision 21 (2026)`. |
